intent.raw_query: Safari Kenya family of 3, $8000, 10 days, July 2026

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming freely against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with iconic savannah landscapes and diverse birdlife.

experiences.name: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park
experiences.description: Explore one of Kenya's few parks on foot or by bicycle, walking among zebras, giraffes, and buffalo without a vehicle. Trek through dramatic gorges, geothermal hot springs, and towering cliffs that inspired the landscapes of Disney's The Lion King. A truly immersive nature experience.
experiences.location: Hell's Gate National Park, Naivasha, Rift Valley

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Visit the alkaline Lake Nakuru, famous for its breathtaking flocks of pink flamingos lining the shores. The surrounding national park is a protected rhino sanctuary housing both black and white rhinos, along with leopards, lions, and over 450 bird species in a compact and accessible reserve.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County, Rift Valley

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience & Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Spend an evening with a traditional Maasai community near the Mara, learning about their ancient customs, warrior traditions, and deep connection to wildlife and land. Participate in traditional dances, visit a boma homestead, and enjoy a authentic bush dinner under the stars with local storytelling around a campfire.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Kenya
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked budget airport shuttle or matatu (local bus) transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Rest and prepare for the adventure ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable - in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable - in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack at the airport arrival hall or a 24-hour convenience store near the resort. Budget: ~500 KES ($4)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer in advance to save money and avoid late-night hassle. Keep small Kenyan shilling notes handy for tips and small purchases. Exchange currency at the airport for convenience, though rates may be slightly lower than city bureaus.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a refreshing morning walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the local coastline, watch local fishermen bring in their morning catch, and breathe in the warm 25°C sea air. Great introduction to Kenya's coastal natural beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby local market to pick up fresh tropical fruits, snacks, and supplies for the trip. Interact with local vendors, practice bargaining, and soak in the vibrant Kenyan coastal culture. Spend time exploring the resort surroundings and nearby nature trails on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset walk along the beach. Watch the stunning Indian Ocean sunset from the beachfront. Head to a local open-air restaurant near the resort for a casual welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast if included, or visit a local 'mama mboga' (street food vendor) for mandazi (fried dough) and chai tea. Budget: ~300 KES ($2.50)
meals.lunch: Fresh tropical fruits and snacks purchased at the local market. Budget: ~400 KES ($3)
meals.dinner: Local coastal restaurant serving grilled fish, ugali, and sukuma wiki (collard greens). Budget: ~800 KES ($6.50)

day_by_day.notes: July is warm and dry along the Kenyan coast with only 30mm of rain expected this month - perfect beach weather. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen. The warm summer weather makes evening walks very pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching session near the resort's beachfront and surrounding vegetation. Kenya's coast is rich with bird species including kingfishers, sunbirds, and herons. Bring binoculars if available or rent a pair locally. This is a free or very low-cost wildlife activity perfect for nature lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget matatu (local minibus) to explore the nearest coastal town. Visit a local nature reserve or community conservation area near the coast. Many offer affordable entry fees and guided walking tours showcasing indigenous coastal forest and wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Join a budget group sunset dhow cruise on the Indian Ocean if available locally - these traditional wooden sailboat trips often cost very little and offer spectacular wildlife spotting opportunities including dolphins.

meals.breakfast: Homemade-style breakfast at a local guesthouse café: eggs, toast, and fresh juice. Budget: ~500 KES ($4)
meals.lunch: Street food from a local kiosk: samosas, chapati, and a cold soda. Budget: ~350 KES ($3)
meals.dinner: Beachside barbecue stall serving grilled prawns or calamari with rice. Budget: ~900 KES ($7.50)

day_by_day.notes: Birdwatching is completely free and highly rewarding along the Kenyan coast. Download a free bird identification app like Merlin before your trip. Matatu rides are extremely affordable - always agree on the fare before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a budget day trip to Tsavo East or Tsavo West National Park, one of Kenya's largest and most accessible wildlife parks. Join a shared budget group safari organized through a local budget tour operator - group safaris significantly reduce per-person costs. Morning game drives offer the best wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive through Tsavo. Look for elephants (Tsavo is famous for its large red-dust-covered elephant herds), lions, giraffes, zebras, buffalos, and hundreds of bird species. Pack a packed lunch to eat at a designated picnic area inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Tsavo to the resort by evening. Rest and freshen up. Share safari stories with fellow travelers at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before departure: bread, peanut butter, and a banana. Budget: ~300 KES ($2.50)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared the night before or purchased at a budget deli: sandwiches, fruit, and water. Budget: ~500 KES ($4)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near the resort: nyama choma (grilled meat) with kachumbari salad and ugali. Budget: ~1000 KES ($8)

day_by_day.notes: Book your budget group safari at least 2-3 days in advance through a reputable local operator. Group safaris of 6-8 people can reduce costs to as low as $40-60 per person including park fees. Bring layers as early morning game drives can be cool despite the warm daytime temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling or reef exploration at a nearby marine park or protected reef area along the coast. Kenya's Indian Ocean coast has vibrant coral reef ecosystems with colorful fish, sea turtles, and marine wildlife. Budget snorkeling gear rental is widely available locally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local community wildlife conservation project or a rescue center for injured wildlife if one is accessible from the resort area. These community-run initiatives often charge minimal entry fees and provide authentic wildlife encounters while supporting local conservation efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local night market or craft market for affordable Kenyan souvenirs such as Maasai beadwork, wooden carvings, and kikoi fabrics. Practice bargaining respectfully for the best prices.

meals.breakfast: Resort café or local spot: uji (porridge) with milk and sugar, a traditional Kenyan breakfast. Budget: ~250 KES ($2)
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut water and a plate of grilled corn from a beach vendor. Budget: ~300 KES ($2.50)
meals.dinner: Swahili cuisine restaurant: coconut fish curry (samaki wa kupaka) with rice. Budget: ~900 KES ($7.50)

day_by_day.notes: Always use reef-safe sunscreen when snorkeling to protect Kenya's fragile coral ecosystems. Check tide times before planning your reef visit - low tide offers the best visibility. The warm 25°C weather makes water activities very comfortable.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day budget safari to Amboseli National Park, famous for its stunning views of Mount Kilimanjaro and large elephant herds. Depart very early morning (5:30-6:00 AM) to maximize game viewing time. Amboseli offers some of Kenya's most iconic wildlife photography opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon game drive in Amboseli. Look for large elephant families at the swamps, as well as lions, cheetahs, wildebeest, and over 400 bird species. The afternoon light is excellent for photography with Kilimanjaro as a backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey from Amboseli to the resort. The drive back offers additional chances to spot roadside wildlife. Arrive back at the resort by late evening.

meals.breakfast: Very early pre-departure breakfast: hard-boiled eggs, bread, and thermos of tea. Budget: ~350 KES ($3)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch at Amboseli's observation hill or picnic site: sandwiches, fruit, and snacks. Budget: ~500 KES ($4)
meals.dinner: Simple self-catered meal at the resort or a nearby local eatery: beans stew with chapati. Budget: ~600 KES ($5)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is approximately 3-4 hours from the coast - this is a long but incredibly rewarding day trip. Consider booking a shared group safari van to split fuel and park entry costs. Park entry fees apply - budget approximately $50-70 per person for a day trip including transport.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after two intensive safari days. Enjoy a slow morning at the beachfront resort. Take a gentle yoga or stretching session on the beach at sunrise. The warm morning temperatures and ocean breeze make this a perfect mindful nature experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local coastal forest or mangrove ecosystem on a self-guided or budget guided walk. Mangrove forests are critical ecosystems teeming with crabs, mudskippers, birds, and unique plant life. Many coastal areas offer free or very low-cost access.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local cultural performance or Swahili music event if available in the area. Many beachfront resorts and local community centers host affordable or free cultural evenings showcasing traditional Kenyan coastal music and dance.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a beachside café: fresh tropical fruit platter, yogurt, and coffee. Budget: ~600 KES ($5)
meals.lunch: Self-catered lunch using market purchases: fresh bread, avocado, tomatoes, and local cheese. Budget: ~400 KES ($3.50)
meals.dinner: Local Swahili restaurant: biryani rice with chicken or vegetables, a coastal Kenyan specialty. Budget: ~850 KES ($7)

day_by_day.notes: Use this rest day to do laundry, recharge camera batteries, back up photos, and plan remaining days. Check in with your budget tour operator to confirm any upcoming bookings. July's dry weather means mangrove walks are comfortable and mud-free.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk through a nearby coastal forest reserve or national monument. Kenya's coastal forests are among the most biodiverse in Africa, home to rare primates like the Sykes monkey and Aders' duiker, as well as hundreds of endemic bird species. Hire a local guide for a very affordable fee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local village or community homestead for a cultural and nature immersion experience. Many coastal communities offer budget-friendly village tours where you can learn about traditional fishing techniques, medicinal plants, and sustainable land use practices.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront bonfire dinner if organized by the resort, or join other travelers for a communal self-catered beach barbecue. Stargaze from the beach - Kenya's clear July skies offer spectacular stargazing with minimal light pollution away from town centers.

meals.breakfast: Local tea house: mandazi doughnuts, boiled eggs, and masala chai. Budget: ~300 KES ($2.50)
meals.lunch: Village community lunch if included in tour, or packed lunch: peanut butter sandwiches and fruit. Budget: ~400 KES ($3.50)
meals.dinner: Self-catered beach barbecue: grilled fish or chicken purchased from local market, with sides. Budget: ~700 KES ($6)

day_by_day.notes: Always hire local guides rather than using outside operators when visiting community areas - this ensures money stays within the local economy. Agree on guide fees upfront. Typical local guide fees range from 500-1500 KES ($4-12) for a half-day walk.

day_by_day.morning: Final wildlife experience: a morning boat trip through a local estuary, creek, or lagoon near the resort. These boat trips offer incredible birdwatching opportunities including flamingos, pelicans, fish eagles, and kingfishers, as well as hippos and crocodiles in some areas. Budget wooden boat trips are very affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beachfront, swimming in the warm Indian Ocean, and reflecting on the trip's wildlife and nature highlights. Take final beach walks and collect memories. Visit any remaining local attractions or viewpoints you haven't yet explored.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best-value local restaurant you've discovered during the trip. Celebrate your Kenya adventure with a special Kenyan meal. Do final souvenir shopping if needed.

meals.breakfast: Pre-boat trip breakfast: fresh juice, tropical fruits, and a boiled egg. Budget: ~400 KES ($3.50)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack: grilled corn, coconut, and cold fresh juice. Budget: ~350 KES ($3)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at best local restaurant: full Kenyan feast with nyama choma, ugali, sukuma wiki, and a cold Tusker beer. Budget: ~1200 KES ($10)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to settle any outstanding resort bills, confirm departure transport arrangements, and pack your bags. Declare any wildlife products (legally purchased crafts) at customs. Never purchase items made from endangered species - this is illegal and unethical.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach for last views of the Indian Ocean. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Complete checkout procedures and gather all luggage. Take final photos of the beachfront and resort surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, use remaining hours for last-minute souvenir shopping at the local market, a final swim, or a relaxed café stop. Arrange budget airport transfer back to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport or the relevant departure airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Kenya with incredible memories of wildlife safaris, coastal nature, and authentic Kenyan culture. Allow extra time at the airport for international departure procedures including security and immigration.

meals.breakfast: Final resort or local breakfast: full Kenyan breakfast with eggs, sausage, toast, and chai. Budget: ~600 KES ($5)
meals.lunch: Airport or departure area meal: light snack or sandwich. Budget: ~700 KES ($6)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Budget approximately 3-4 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some Kenyan shillings for airport snacks and tips but note that unspent KES can be exchanged back at the airport. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations. Kenya departure tax is typically included in your flight ticket.

trip_options.title: Classic Kenya Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle into Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal
meals.lunch: In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange an airport transfer with the resort in advance. Keep essentials like travel documents, chargers, and a change of clothes in your carry-on for a smooth arrival. Exchange some currency to Kenyan Shillings (KES) at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a relaxed orientation walk along the beachfront to get acquainted with the surroundings and recover from jet lag.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local coastal area near the resort — stroll through nearby markets, pick up any essentials, and soak in the warm Kenyan coastal atmosphere. Visit a local curio shop to browse handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset view from the resort's beachfront terrace. Have a relaxed dinner at the resort restaurant and plan the upcoming safari days ahead with your itinerary.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and Kenyan chai
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a nearby coastal café — try Swahili dishes like pilau rice or grilled fish (budget ~$10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — opt for a grilled seafood platter or Nyama Choma (roasted meat) with ugali (budget ~$20–25 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery day — do not over-schedule. Hydrate well and apply sunscreen as temperatures will reach around 25°C. Confirm all upcoming safari bookings and transfers with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by road or chartered flight to Amboseli National Park. Check into a mid-range safari lodge or tented camp near the park. Begin the Amboseli Elephant Watching experience with a morning game drive — spot large elephant herds roaming the plains with the iconic snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro as a backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your afternoon game drive through Amboseli, exploring the wetlands and observation hills. Look out for lions, cheetahs, hippos, and hundreds of bird species. Visit Observation Hill for panoramic views of the park and Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for sundowner drinks at dusk. Enjoy a communal bush-style dinner around a campfire at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — packed breakfast box if leaving very early
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch provided by the lodge during the afternoon game drive
meals.dinner: Set dinner menu at the Amboseli safari lodge — expect hearty African stews, grilled meats, and seasonal vegetables (included in lodge package or ~$25–35 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Amboseli is approximately a 4–5 hour drive from Nairobi or a 45-minute charter flight. July is peak dry season — excellent visibility and wildlife concentration around water sources. Bring binoculars, a zoom camera lens, and dust covers for your gear.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a sunrise game drive in Amboseli — the golden morning light against Kilimanjaro is world-class for photography. Spot elephants, buffaloes, and wildebeest active in the cool morning air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Maasai community near Amboseli for a cultural interaction — learn about traditional Maasai life, beadwork, and cattle herding. Browse and purchase handmade jewelry and crafts directly from artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Amboseli and transfer to Lake Nakuru region (approximately 4–5 hours by road via Nairobi, or arrange an internal flight). Check into a mid-range lodge near Lake Nakuru National Park.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the sunrise drive — hot tea/coffee and toast
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge or a roadside restaurant during the transfer — try Kenyan beef stew or chapati with beans (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Lake Nakuru area lodge — buffet-style with a variety of Kenyan and continental options (~$20–30 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Maasai village visit typically costs around $20–30 USD per person — negotiate respectfully and always ask permission before photographing community members. Confirm your Lake Nakuru accommodation ahead of time as July is high season.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit. Start with a morning game drive inside Lake Nakuru National Park. Witness the spectacular sight of thousands of pink flamingos lining the alkaline lake shores, creating a breathtaking pink carpet effect.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lake Nakuru — search for both black and white rhinos (the park is a key rhino sanctuary), leopards resting in yellow fever trees, and large troops of baboons. Visit the Baboon Cliff viewpoint for sweeping panoramic views of the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a relaxed evening. Optional sundowner walk on the lodge grounds with a naturalist guide. Enjoy dinner and swap wildlife stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the lodge before the morning drive
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed at a designated picnic site within Lake Nakuru National Park
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge — try tilapia fish from Lake Victoria, nyama choma, and fresh vegetable sides (~$20–28 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru National Park entrance fees are approximately $60 USD per person per day for non-residents — budget accordingly. The flamingo numbers can vary seasonally but July typically offers good sightings. Rhino tracking is a highlight — ask your guide to prioritize rhino areas.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Lake Nakuru and drive approximately 1.5–2 hours to Hell's Gate National Park near Naivasha. Begin the Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate — explore dramatic gorges, towering cliffs, and geothermal steam vents entirely on foot or by bicycle (rentals available at the gate).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Hell's Gate experience — walk among zebras, giraffes, buffaloes, and warthogs roaming freely without fences. Descend into the spectacular Hell's Gate Gorge with your guide for a unique geological and wildlife experience. Visit the Fischer's Tower rock column.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to a mid-range lodge or camp near Naivasha or begin the drive toward the Maasai Mara region. Check into your Mara-area accommodation and enjoy a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Lake Nakuru lodge before checkout
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a local restaurant in Naivasha town — try a hearty Kenyan lunch of ugali, sukuma wiki (collard greens), and grilled chicken (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at your Naivasha or Mara-area lodge — grilled meats and local vegetable dishes (~$20–25 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate National Park entrance is approximately $25 USD per person — one of Kenya's most affordable parks. Bicycle hire costs around $5–10 USD. Wear closed-toe shoes, carry water, and apply sunscreen. The gorge walk requires a local guide (arranged at the gate) for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in the Maasai Mara ecosystem and begin the iconic Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari. Start with a full morning game drive — July is peak Great Migration season. Witness massive herds of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles moving across the golden savannah in one of nature's greatest spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the afternoon game drive focusing on predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are highly active during the Migration as they follow the herds. Cross into the Mara Triangle if your guide recommends it for the best Migration river crossing viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for a sundowner on the Mara plains. Enjoy a bush dinner under the stars — a magical Mara evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at camp — packed breakfast enjoyed on the Mara plains during the morning drive
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at a scenic Mara viewpoint
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Mara camp or lodge — barbecued meats, African salads, and local desserts around a bonfire (~$25–35 USD or included in lodge package)

day_by_day.notes: July is arguably the best month to witness the Great Migration river crossings at the Mara River. Patience is key — crossings can happen at any time and are unpredictable. Communicate with your guide to position yourselves at the river early. A mid-range tented camp in the Mara costs approximately $150–250 USD per night including meals and game drives.

day_by_day.morning: Optional early morning hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise (premium add-on, approximately $450–500 USD per person — book well in advance). Alternatively, enjoy a pre-dawn game drive to catch predators on early morning hunts across the open plains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maasai Cultural Village Experience — spend time with a traditional Maasai community near the Mara. Participate in traditional dances, learn about Maasai warrior customs, visit a traditional manyatta (homestead), and try your hand at fire-making and beadwork.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Bush Dinner experience — enjoy a specially prepared bush dinner in the wild, surrounded by the sounds of the African night, with Maasai guides sharing stories of their ancestral lands under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in the bush following the balloon safari, or full breakfast at camp
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Maasai village or camp — traditional Maasai tea (sweet milky chai) and simple snacks
meals.dinner: Traditional Maasai Bush Dinner — roasted meats, African stews, and fresh bread prepared in the bush (~$40–60 USD per person as a special experience, or included in some lodge packages)

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon safari must be booked well in advance — contact your lodge or a reputable operator like Governors' Balloon Safaris. The Maasai cultural experience typically costs $30–50 USD per person. Bring small denomination KES notes as tips for village hosts and dancers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning game drive in the Maasai Mara — make the most of your last hours in this world-class ecosystem. Focus on any wildlife you haven't yet seen, or revisit the Mara River for one more chance at a wildebeest crossing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the Maasai Mara and transfer back toward Nairobi (approximately 5–6 hours by road or 45 minutes by charter flight). Check back into a Nairobi hotel or return to the coastal resort. Use the afternoon to visit the Nairobi Giraffe Centre (if routing through Nairobi) — hand-feed endangered Rothschild giraffes in a fun and accessible experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner in Nairobi at a mid-range restaurant celebrating the incredible safari journey. Alternatively, return to Aegean Bliss Resort on the coast for a relaxing beachfront evening.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Mara camp before checkout
meals.lunch: Roadside or restaurant stop during transfer — try a local Kenyan buffet restaurant (kariokor-style) for an authentic experience (~$8–12 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a recommended Nairobi restaurant such as Carnivore Restaurant (famous for game meats) or Talisman Restaurant for a more refined mid-range experience (~$25–40 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Giraffe Centre in Nairobi is open daily and costs approximately $15 USD per adult — a wonderful and photogenic experience. If flying back to the coast, book your internal flight in advance with operators like Safarilink or AirKenya. Confirm your return transfer to the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront (if not already there). Enjoy a final leisurely morning on the Kenyan coast — swim in the Indian Ocean, relax on the beach, or enjoy a beachside yoga or meditation session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a nearby coastal market — pick up Maasai beadwork, wooden carvings, kikoi fabrics, or Kenyan coffee and tea to bring home. Enjoy a final coastal stroll and take in the warm Kenyan sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort or a highly-rated local coastal restaurant — celebrate 10 incredible days in Kenya with a feast of fresh Swahili seafood. Pack bags and prepare for departure or onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, coconut bread, Kenyan coffee, and eggs cooked to order
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort or a nearby seafood shack — grilled prawns, calamari, and cold Tusker beer (~$15–20 USD)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant or a local Swahili restaurant — try full Swahili seafood platter with coconut rice, tamarind sauce, and fresh mango dessert (~$25–35 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time for packing and checkout formalities. If your departure flight is the next day, confirm your airport transfer time. Keep a small amount of KES for tips to resort staff who made your stay memorable. Kenya's tipping culture: 10–15% at restaurants, $5–10 USD per day for safari guides and drivers is greatly appreciated.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Kenya Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari
experiences.description: Witness the world-famous Great Migration where millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles cross the Mara River in a dramatic spectacle. Game drives in open 4x4 vehicles offer close encounters with the Big Five including lions, elephants, leopards, buffaloes, and rhinos in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Maasai Mara National Reserve, Narok County

experiences.name: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views
experiences.description: Observe some of Africa's largest elephant herds roaming freely against the stunning backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro. Amboseli is renowned for its large elephant population and offers exceptional photography opportunities with iconic savannah landscapes and diverse birdlife.

experiences.name: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park
experiences.description: Explore one of Kenya's few parks on foot or by bicycle, walking among zebras, giraffes, and buffalo without a vehicle. Trek through dramatic gorges, geothermal hot springs, and towering cliffs that inspired the landscapes of Disney's The Lion King. A truly immersive nature experience.
experiences.location: Hell's Gate National Park, Naivasha, Rift Valley

experiences.name: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit
experiences.description: Visit the alkaline Lake Nakuru, famous for its breathtaking flocks of pink flamingos lining the shores. The surrounding national park is a protected rhino sanctuary housing both black and white rhinos, along with leopards, lions, and over 450 bird species in a compact and accessible reserve.
experiences.location: Lake Nakuru National Park, Nakuru County, Rift Valley

experiences.name: Maasai Cultural Village Experience & Bush Dinner
experiences.description: Spend an evening with a traditional Maasai community near the Mara, learning about their ancient customs, warrior traditions, and deep connection to wildlife and land. Participate in traditional dances, visit a boma homestead, and enjoy a authentic bush dinner under the stars with local storytelling around a campfire.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Nairobi Jomo Kenyatta International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A dedicated luxury transfer driver will meet you at arrivals with a name board. Private chauffeur-driven vehicle transports you to your first-night stay at a premium Nairobi airport hotel (e.g., Trademark Hotel or Fairmont The Norfolk). Check in, unwind, and enjoy a welcome drink at the bar.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night supper at the hotel's 24-hour dining service — charcuterie board, artisan sandwiches, and a glass of South African Chenin Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely an arrival day. No sightseeing is planned. Confirm luggage collection and porter assistance in advance. Keep travel documents and accommodation vouchers accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel before a private guided morning tour of Nairobi's highlights — visit the iconic Giraffe Centre to hand-feed endangered Rothschild giraffes, followed by a stop at the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust elephant orphanage for the 11:00 AM public feeding hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer (approximately 6 hours) to the Maasai Mara region. Journey through the Great Rift Valley with a scenic viewpoint stop at the escarpment. Arrive at your luxury tented camp (e.g., Angama Mara or Mahali Mzuri) in time for check-in and a camp orientation tour.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on the camp's panoramic viewing deck overlooking the Mara plains. Settle into your luxury tent and enjoy a welcome dinner under the stars at the camp's open-air dining area.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the Nairobi hotel — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruit platter, Kenyan AA coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch box prepared by the hotel, enjoyed at the Rift Valley viewpoint during the transfer
meals.dinner: Three-course welcome dinner at the luxury tented camp — roasted bush vegetables, slow-braised game meat, and a classic African malva pudding paired with Kenyan wines

day_by_day.notes: Pack a light safari bag for the Mara camp as luggage weight restrictions may apply on any light aircraft upgrades. Bring binoculars, sunscreen SPF 50+, and a light fleece for cool Mara evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up call for a full-day Maasai Mara Great Migration Safari. Board a private 4x4 Land Cruiser with your expert guide at 06:00. Witness the extraordinary spectacle of millions of wildebeest and zebras moving across the golden savannah. Position near the Mara River crossings for dramatic predator-prey interaction sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Great Migration safari through the afternoon. Enjoy a luxury bush picnic lunch set up by your camp team in the heart of the Mara. Look out for the Big Five — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo, and rhino — as predator activity peaks in the afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp at sunset for a hot outdoor shower and relaxation. Attend a private stargazing session with the camp's resident astronomer, identifying southern hemisphere constellations above the Mara.

meals.breakfast: Early bush breakfast at camp before departure — fresh pastries, boiled eggs, seasonal fruit, and strong Kenyan coffee served in the open air
meals.lunch: Luxury white-glove bush picnic — chilled gazpacho, gourmet wraps, cheese selection, and sparkling water served on linen tablecloths in the savannah
meals.dinner: Candlelit four-course dinner at the camp — roasted bone marrow, pan-seared impala loin, passion fruit soufflé, and a curated Kenyan honey wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: July is peak Great Migration season — river crossings are most frequent in the morning. Ask your guide to radio other guides for real-time crossing alerts. Dress in neutral earth tones (khaki, olive, beige) to avoid disturbing wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara at sunrise (approximately 06:00–08:30). Drift silently above the migration herds, spotting wildlife from a bird's-eye perspective with breathtaking golden-hour lighting. A champagne breakfast is served in the bush upon landing — a signature Mara experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to camp for a midday rest and spa treatment. Enjoy a traditional Maasai-inspired massage or a signature African botanical body wrap at the camp's luxury wellness tent. Optional afternoon game drive for those seeking more wildlife time.
day_by_day.evening: Maasai Cultural Village Experience & Bush Dinner. Transfer to a traditional Maasai enkang (village) near the Mara. Participate in warrior jumping dances, beadwork demonstrations, and fire-making rituals. A spectacular bush dinner is served under acacia trees with Maasai elders sharing stories of their ancient customs.

meals.breakfast: Champagne bush breakfast post-balloon landing — smoked salmon blinis, fresh fruit, croissants, and Moët & Chandon Brut
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at camp — grilled fish tacos, avocado salad, and freshly squeezed mango juice
meals.dinner: Traditional Maasai bush dinner — nyama choma (roasted goat), ugali, sukuma wiki, and honey-fermented mead served around a roaring bonfire

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon bookings must be confirmed at least 48 hours in advance and are subject to weather conditions. Balloon flights typically last 60–90 minutes. Wear warm layers as early morning temperatures at altitude can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning game drive focusing on predator activity — lions, cheetahs, and leopards are most active at dawn. Visit the Mara Triangle for less-crowded sightings and pristine landscapes managed by the Mara Conservancy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer (approximately 4 hours) or scenic charter flight from Mara to Amboseli National Park. Check in to your exclusive lodge (e.g., Ol Tukai Lodge or Tortilis Camp) with iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset game drive in Amboseli with your private guide. Amboseli's open plains offer exceptional photographic opportunities of elephants silhouetted against Kilimanjaro at dusk. Return to lodge for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full camp breakfast — Kenyan mandazi doughnuts, fresh papaya, scrambled eggs with herbs, and strong Kenyan tea
meals.lunch: En route lunch at a premium roadside lodge restaurant or packed gourmet lunch box — artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge's signature restaurant — slow-cooked Amboseli lamb, roasted root vegetables, and a decadent dark chocolate tart with Kilimanjaro coffee

day_by_day.notes: If opting for a charter flight from Mara to Amboseli, the scenic 45-minute flight offers spectacular aerial views of the Rift Valley. Luggage weight restrictions of 15 kg in soft bags apply on light aircraft.

day_by_day.morning: Amboseli Elephant Watching with Kilimanjaro Views — embark on a dedicated full-morning elephant safari with your private guide. Amboseli is home to some of Africa's most studied and largest elephant herds. Observe matriarchs leading their families across the swamps with the snow-capped peak of Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) as a dramatic backdrop. Photography enthusiasts will find this a world-class opportunity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Amboseli Observation Hill for panoramic 360-degree views of the park. Spend the afternoon at leisure at the lodge — use the swimming pool, enjoy a spa treatment, or join a guided nature walk around the lodge grounds with a Maasai guide.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner experience on the open plains — your lodge team sets up a bespoke cocktail station at a scenic location as the sun dips behind Kilimanjaro. Return for a gourmet dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast on your private lodge terrace — eggs to order, smoked meats, seasonal fruits, and freshly brewed Kenyan single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the lodge — grilled Nile perch, quinoa salad with pomegranate, and chilled hibiscus iced tea
meals.dinner: Six-course tasting menu at the lodge's fine dining venue — featuring locally sourced ingredients including Amboseli honey, organic vegetables, and free-range meats, paired with South African wines

day_by_day.notes: Kilimanjaro's summit is most visible in the early morning before clouds build — plan the elephant safari for 06:00–09:00 for the best photographic conditions. Bring a telephoto lens (at least 300mm) for wildlife photography.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Amboseli for a private transfer to Lake Nakuru National Park (approximately 4–5 hours via Nairobi). Stop in Nairobi for a brief break and shopping opportunity at the upscale Village Market or Karen Blixen Museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Nakuru and check in to your luxury lodge (e.g., Sarova Lion Hill Game Lodge or Mbweha Camp). Afternoon game drive to the shores of Lake Nakuru for the first sighting of its legendary pink flamingo flocks and the park's thriving rhino sanctuary.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks on the lodge's elevated terrace overlooking the lake. The alkaline waters reflect the pink hues of flamingos at dusk — a truly unforgettable scene. Dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at Amboseli lodge before departure — fresh pastries, yoghurt, tropical fruits, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Talisman Restaurant in Karen, Nairobi — a beloved premium dining institution known for its eclectic global menu and lush garden setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Nakuru lodge — pan-fried tilapia from Lake Victoria, roasted plantain, and a classic Kenyan chai crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: Lake Nakuru's flamingo population fluctuates seasonally depending on algae levels. July typically offers excellent sightings. The park is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Kenya's premier rhino sanctuaries for both black and white rhinos.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Nakuru Flamingo & Rhino Sanctuary Visit — full morning game drive along the lake's shoreline. Witness up to one million lesser and greater flamingos creating a breathtaking pink carpet along the water's edge. Track both black and white rhinos with your expert guide — Lake Nakuru is one of Kenya's most reliable rhino-spotting destinations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided Walking Safari in Hell's Gate National Park (approximately 1 hour from Nakuru). Explore one of Kenya's only parks on foot or by bicycle — walk among zebras, giraffes, and buffalo in the dramatic volcanic gorge landscape. Hell's Gate was the inspiration for Disney's 'The Lion King' scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Nakuru lodge for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private in-room spa treatment or soak in your lodge's outdoor plunge pool. A special private dining experience is arranged on the lodge's viewing deck.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — Kenyan githeri (corn and beans), fresh fruit, eggs Benedict, and freshly squeezed passion fruit juice
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Hell's Gate — gourmet packed boxes with artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and sparkling water enjoyed at Fischer's Tower viewpoint
meals.dinner: Private deck dinner at the lodge — slow-braised ostrich fillet, truffle mashed potatoes, grilled asparagus, and a decadent tiramisu with Kenyan espresso

day_by_day.notes: Hell's Gate National Park allows walking and cycling without a guide — a rare and exhilarating experience in East Africa. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes and carry at least 2 litres of water. The gorge walk takes approximately 2 hours and involves some scrambling.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the Nakuru lodge — optional early birdwatching walk with the lodge's resident ornithologist. Lake Nakuru is a birder's paradise with over 450 recorded species including African fish eagles, pelicans, and cormorants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Nairobi (approximately 2.5 hours). Check in to your final Nairobi hotel (e.g., Fairmont The Norfolk or The Hemingways Nairobi) for your last night before flying to the coast. Afternoon at leisure — visit the upscale Westgate Shopping Mall or relax at the hotel's spa.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Nairobi's finest restaurants — Carnivore Restaurant for a legendary African game meat feast, or Talisman Karen for a refined international dining experience. Celebrate the journey with premium cocktails at the hotel's rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast at Nakuru — full Kenyan spread including mandazi, fresh tropical fruits, scrambled eggs, and Kenyan masala chai
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Nairobi hotel's brasserie upon arrival — club sandwich, Caesar salad, and fresh mango sorbet
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Carnivore Restaurant, Nairobi — the legendary 'Beast of a Feast' featuring nyama choma of crocodile, ostrich, and game meats carved tableside, paired with Kenyan Dawa cocktails (vodka, honey, and lime)

day_by_day.notes: Carnivore Restaurant is an iconic Nairobi institution and a must-experience for meat lovers. Vegetarian options are available. Reserve well in advance as it is extremely popular. The Dawa cocktail is Carnivore's signature drink — do not leave without trying one.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nairobi — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Optional visit to the Karen Blixen Museum (Out of Africa author's former home) or a last-minute souvenir shopping trip to the Kazuri Beads workshop or Utamaduni Craft Centre for authentic Kenyan crafts and jewellery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for your onward flight to the Kenyan coast (Mombasa or Diani Beach) to check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, Kenya. Upon arrival at the coast, a resort representative meets you for a seamless beachfront check-in experience. Spend the afternoon settling in, exploring the resort, and unwinding on the pristine Indian Ocean beach.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy fresh Swahili Coast cuisine featuring grilled lobster, coconut prawn curry, and pilau rice as the Indian Ocean breeze rolls in. Toast to an extraordinary 10-day Kenyan adventure with a sundowner of fresh coconut water and premium rum on the beachfront terrace.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast in Nairobi — smoked salmon bagels, Belgian waffles with Kenyan honey, fresh fruit platter, and a farewell cup of Kenya AA single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or en route — mezze platter, fresh salad, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Beachfront welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — Swahili-spiced grilled lobster, coconut fish curry, freshly baked chapati, and a tropical passion fruit panna cotta, paired with chilled Kenyan white wine

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your coastal transfer or flight booking from Nairobi to Mombasa/Ukunda airstrip in advance. The flight is approximately 1 hour. Alternatively, a luxury road transfer takes 8–9 hours via Mombasa Highway. Pack light breathable clothing for the warm and humid coastal climate (average 25°C). Apply reef-safe sunscreen at the beach resort.
